meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale, and I'd like to know why my son's zero was in the gradebook before anyone called me.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what was it based on?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
I'm writing down "isn't anywhere in Hamlet." Which page of the essay is it on, and what did you check it against? A misquote isn't a zero, Hale.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. Claire's case is the reason the principal is my next stop, and you still haven't answered what you checked that line against.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn and a written answer on what you checked that line against. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: the opening position, with the zero still standing and nothing agreed.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero", because it owned the process failure plainly and got her a small step toward listening.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family", because it brought up Claire and pushed her toward the principal.
Try next time: when she asked what you checked the line against, answer that with the page and the source you used instead of reaching for her family's history.
